seed_problem: A set of auctions with bids, participant identities, and cost covariates; solver flags cartel sets; checker scores detection F1 against hidden collusion; flagging high bids fails on plausible-range cartels.
title: Bidders Who Agreed Beforehand
mutation: composite: goal becomes a graded, F1-based bidder-flagging-and-grouping quality metric (not a decision problem); the intended solution must recover a per-bidder COST-CONSISTENCY statistic (implied rate = bid / job-size, must stay constant across auctions for an honest bidder) rather than an outlierness threshold, because ROTATING cover bids keep every bid in the plausible range while breaking single-rate consistency.
innovation_hook: Flagging unusually high bids catches nothing because cartel cover bids are priced off the CURRENT rotating winner's rate plus a small markup, so they never look like outliers; the insight is that this rotation makes a ring member's IMPLIED PER-UNIT RATE (bid / job size) inconsistent across auctions even though the bid LEVEL stays plausible -- a designed cost-consistency screening statistic exposes this where raw-bid thresholding cannot.
strategies: trivial: flag only the single highest total-bid bidder per market as an ungrouped singleton (the grader's own baseline construction) -> ratio ~0.1

greedy (trap): sort bidders by average bid and flag the top ~35% as ONE group, i.e. 'unusually high bidders are the cartel' -- this is defeated by (a) legitimately expensive honest bidders who out-bid ring members in level, and (b) ring cover bids that are deliberately NOT outliers

strong: for each bidder compute the set of implied rates floor(bid_a / s_a) over all its auctions; a bidder whose implied-rate set has more than one distinct value is flagged (this exactly identifies a rotating ring member, since an honest bidder's implied rate is provably constant while a cover-bidding ring member's is not); group every flagged bidder of a market into one claimed ring (at most one ring exists per market)

further headroom: the baseline is deliberately calibrated low (a raw-bid-level reference), so even the exact cost-consistency detector leaves visible ratio headroom below the 1.0 cap; a still-stronger policy could additionally cross-check WHICH other bidder's rate a cover bid tracks each round to disambiguate markets seeded with two overlapping decoy patterns
